rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere believers wanted a revealed surah because their faith and piety were increasing, and they longed for permission to fight disbelievers' error and tyranny.
rows.anchor: hâllerinde günden güne salâh artmış, imanlarında sâdık hâlis mü’minler kâfirlerin dalâl ve tuğyânı karşısında takvâ hislerinin izdiyâdıyla fî sebîlillah cihâda izin verilmesini arzu ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fighting surah is muhkam either because the duty to fight is stated clearly beyond ambiguity, or because its ruling is established and unabrogated.
rows.anchor: kıtâlin vücûbu teşâbüh ve ihtimalden ârî sağlam bir surette beyan olunan bir sûre, yahut hükmü sâbit gayr-i mensuh bir sûre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the fighting passages in al-Baqara, al-Anfāl, and Barāʾa as muhkam, and says the fighting verses remain fixed until war lays down its burdens.
rows.anchor: Âyât-ı kıtâl حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا sâbittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sickness in the hearts means either hypocrisy or weakness in religion.
rows.anchor: bir nifak, yahut din zayıflığı bulunanları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' gaze resembles that of someone fainting at death: they can barely raise their eyes and glance fearfully sideways.
rows.anchor: gözünü açmaya dermanı olmayan bir muhtazar gibi baygın baygın gözlerini kaldıramıyor, yan yan bakıyorlar, öyle korkuyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of fa-awlā lahum is that death would be more suitable for such people than life.
rows.anchor: öyle kimselere de ölüm yaşamaktan daha evlâ daha münâsibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fa-awlā is a superlative from wail: the most terrifying destruction is theirs.
rows.anchor: Yahut “veyl”den ism-i tafdîl olarak veylin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallaytum can mean turning back and fleeing, or taking charge as governor; both interpretations are sound.
rows.anchor: Birisi arkasını dönüp kaçmak mânasına “tevellî”den, birisi de “velâyet”ten tefe‘‘ul olarak vâli olmak, iş başına geçmek mânasına tefsir olunmuştur. Binâen‘aleyh şu iki mânanın ikisi de doğrudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahim literally means the womb, then denotes kinship because kinship originates through it; here erham means relatives.
rows.anchor: “Rahim” esasen kadının çocuk makarrı olan cihâzıdır. Karâbet menşe’i olmak hasebiyle akrabalığa da “rahim” ıtlak olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the fleeing reading, retreating from battle disrupts the army, enables enemy occupation, and exposes wives, children, and relatives to slaughter.
rows.anchor: Müslüman ordusunda fesat çıkarıp düşman istîlâsına sebebiyet verildiği takdirde hâsıl olacak netice budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the governing reading, taking command could ruin the homeland as in the age of ignorance and leave relatives in civil turmoil.
rows.anchor: iş başına geçer, kumandayı elinize alır da vatanınızı câhiliye devri gibi fesâda verir, ihtilâl içinde hısım ve akrabalarınızı yine öyle perişan edebilir misiniz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse serves as evidence that severing family ties is forbidden.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetle kat‘-ı rahimin hurmetine istidlâl olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke is followed by a shift in address to show that these people are unworthy even of being addressed by way of reproach.
rows.anchor: Burada bunları bu suretle tevbih ederken, böyle tevbih tarîkiyle bile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described are people whom God cursed and expelled from the reach of His mercy.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın lânet ettiği; rahmeti sahasından tard eylediği kimselerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deafens their ears and blinds their eyes; they neither hear the true word nor see signs in themselves and the world because they refuse to look.
rows.anchor: Hak kelâmını işitmezler, enfüs ü âfâktaki âyât-ı hakkı görmezler, bakmak istemedikleri için görmezler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about pondering the Qur'an is a rhetorical confirmation, fitting the context's implication that God has sealed their hearts.
rows.anchor: Bunun طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ mazmûnu üzere istifhâm-ı takrîrî olması siyâka daha münâsibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cadence in aqluhā recalls the earlier cadence amthāluhā and warns the reader not to overlook the connection.
rows.anchor: أَقْفَالُهَآ fâsılası tâ yukarıdaki وَلِلْكَٰفِرِينَ أَمْثَٰلُهَا fâsılasına nâzırdır, onu ihtar eder, gaflet olunmaya.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan made major sins seem insignificant to them and incited them to pursue their passions.
rows.anchor: Büyük günahları ehemmiyetsiz göstererek şehevâta saldırttı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan also filled them with desires and long hopes.
rows.anchor: ve onları arzu ve emellere düşürdü.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disliked revelation include the Jews of Banū Qurayẓa and Banū Naḍīr, while Quraysh polytheists objected that the Qur'an should have come to a great man from either town.
rows.anchor: Benî Kureyza ve Benî Nadîr Yahudîleri Hazret-i Peygamber’e Kur’ân’ın indirilmesini hoşlanmamışlardı. Kureyş müşrikleri de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites secretly promised those Jews or polytheists obedience in some matters; their pact also recalls the promise to support the People of the Book in al-Hashr and their alliance at the Battle of the Confederates.
rows.anchor: münafıklar o Yahudîlere veya müşriklere gizlice söz vererek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew their secret conversations, yet they disregarded this and secretly conspired against God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki Allah onların o gizli konuşmalarını biliyordu. Öyle iken onu hesâba almadılar da Allah’a ve Peygamberine karşı gizli ittifâka kalkıştılar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihbāt removes a deed's reward and reduces it to nothing; good deeds can expiate and cover bad deeds, while bad deeds annul good ones, making ihbāt the opposite of expiation and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: “İhbât” amelin sevâbını giderip hiçe indirmektir. Güzel amel, günaha keffâret olup kötü ameli örttüğü gibi kötü ameller de iyi amelleri ihbat eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites did have good deeds, but they did things that incurred God's anger and disliked His approval, so their good works were nullified.
rows.anchor: onların iyi amelleri de yok değildi, fakat Allah’ın gazabını davet eden şeyler yapıp rıdvânını kerih gördüklerinden dolayı iyi amelleri habt olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest opening is a conquest that opens the future and begins many conquests to come.
rows.anchor: istikbâli açan, ileride vukū‘bulacak birçok fetihlerin mebde’i olan bir fetih.

rows.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes understood the opening as a promise of the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirîn bunu Mekke’nin fethini vaad diye telakkī etmişlerse de

rows.speaker: cumhur
rows.claim: The majority identifies the opening as news of the Hudaybiyya treaty; this was also narrated from Ibn Abbas, Anas, al-Shaʿbī, and al-Zuhrī.
rows.anchor: cumhur bunun Hudeybiye sulhunu ihbar olduğunu söylemişler; İbn Abbas, Enes, Şa‘bî ve Zührî’den de böyle rivayet eylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the Hudaybiyya interpretation correct.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye buna وَهُوَ ال َّصحِيح demiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fath lexically means opening or removing closure; conquest of a country is victory achieved by war or peace, by force or treaty, as al-Kashshāf explains.
rows.anchor: “feth” aslında açmak, yani kapalılığı gidermektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudaybiyya could seem to contradict the command not to weaken or call for peace while superior; even some Companions failed to see its victory, so God explicitly calls it manifest.
rows.anchor: Hudeybiye sulhunun bir fetih olması ashabdan bazılarına bile hafî kalmıştı. Cenâb-ı Allah bunun bir feth-i mübîn olduğunu beyan buyurmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet set out for ʿumra with sacrificial animals rather than battle, the polytheists prepared to fight; the Muslims defeated them after exchanges of arrows and stones, and the polytheists sought a treaty.
rows.anchor: Peygamber bunda bir harb için değil, bir umre niyetiyle hareket etmiş ve kurbanlıklar sevkeylemişti, fakat müşrikler çarpışmayı kurmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treaty made Islam's existence as a polity recognized by its enemies and bound by a formal agreement.
rows.anchor: ilk evvel Müslümanlığın âlemde bir devlet olarak mevcûdiyeti düşmanları tarafından dahi tasdik olunarak bir mukaveleye rabt edilmiş bulunuyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudaybiyya became the beginning of an ensuing series of conquests; Khaybar followed soon, then Mecca, and Islam's supremacy over all religions was promised.
rows.anchor: bunu pek yakından Hayber fethi tâkip etmiş, sonra da Mekke fetholunmuş

rows.speaker: Zührî
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī says no conquest was greater than Hudaybiyya: contact with Muslims let polytheists hear their message, which took root and led many to convert within three years.
rows.anchor: Zührî demiştir ki: “Hudeybiye fethinden büyük bir fetih olmamıştır. Bu sayede müşrikler Müslümanlarla ihtilâta girişmiş ve sözlerini işitmeye başlamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attributes these outcomes to the blessed effects of the rulings in the opening verses of Sūrat Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: Bütün bunlar Sûre-i Muhammed’in başında geçen âyetlerin feyz-i hükmüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubīn means clear, bright, or opening and showing what lies ahead.
rows.anchor: “Mübîn” açık, parlak, yahut ilerisini açan gösteren demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifestness of the conquest has four combined outcomes: forgiveness, completion of blessing, guidance to a straight path, and mighty victory; the lām in li-yaghfira marks an ultimate outcome or wisdom.
rows.anchor: bunların her birini ayrıca değil mecmû‘unu birden bir hikmet olmak üzere bir lâm-ı âkıbet ile şöyle buyuruyor

rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī explains forgiveness as the ultimate wisdom of conquest: jihad removes shirk and raises religion, guides deficient souls toward perfection, and rescues the weak from oppressors.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî der ki: “Fetih küffâra cihad ile şirkin def‘ine ve dinin i‘lâsına ve nüfûs-ı nâkısanın tedrîcen ihtiyarlarıyla tekemmül edebilmeleri için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām expresses a final wisdom, so this conquest and forgiveness are the response and fruit of the command in Muḥammad 47:19 to seek forgiveness for the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: buradaki feth u mağfiret Sûre-i Muhammed’deki

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the shift from God's majestic We for opening to the divine name for forgiveness may imply that God uses means for victory but forgives directly Himself.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Fetih إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا diye azamet nûnuyla isnad olunduktan sonra mağfiretin لِّيَغْفِرَ لَكَ ٱللَّهُ diye ism-i celâl ile isnad olunması şu nükteye işaret olabilir

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some say the great use the first-person plural because their actions usually employ assistants and followers; Elmalılı says attributing victory to God by name does not refute this.
rows.anchor: Buna nasrın وَيَنصُرَكَ ٱللَّهُ diye ism-i celîle isnad olunmasıyla itiraz da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı finds it clearer that the wording points to the truths that victory comes only from God and only God forgives sins.
rows.anchor: hakikatlerine işaret olunmuş demek daha açık olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past and future sins together are a figure for all sins; the Prophet is thus proclaimed purified and absolved of every sin.
rows.anchor: Zenbin mâtekaddem ve mâteahharı, geçmişi ve geleceği hepsini ihâtadan kinayedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past suggests an actual sin while future suggests a hypothetical one, prompting discussion of what sin could be attributed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: “mâtekaddem” tâbiri zenbin vukū‘unu iş‘âr ederse de, “mâteahhar” tâbiri

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArabī and others say the sin meant is that of the community; direct addresses to the Prophet in 10:94 and 39:65 can implicitly address the community, but this reading does not fit 47:19.
rows.anchor: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî gibi bazıları murad, ümmetin zenbi olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some hold that no actual sin is intended; the whole construction indirectly promises that the Prophet will not be held accountable.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da demişlerdir ki zenbin vukū‘u murad olmayarak terkîbin hey’et-i mecmû‘ası ‘adem-i muâhazeden kinayedir.

rows.speaker: ekser müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand the sins as choices in matters without revelation that are less than best relative to prophethood, as in the admonition of 9:43; calling them sins is relative to that station, since the righteous' good deeds count as sins for the near ones.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin kavlince ise vahiy vârid olmayan husûsâttaki ictihâdâtında makāmına nisbetle hilâf-ı evlâ kabîlinden olan ihtiyarlarıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This implies that the earlier hardships and obstacles in carrying out the prophetic mission will no longer weigh on him, as expressed in al-Inshirāḥ 94:2–3.
rows.anchor: Buradan bundan böyle risalet vazifesinin îfâsında evvelki mihen ü mezâhimin ağırlığı kalmayacağına da istidlâl olunabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the fruits of the mission begin to be gathered, its difficulties are covered by the joy of success.
rows.anchor: Semerâtı iktitaf olunmaya başlayan vazifelerin müşkilâtı muvaffakiyet neş’eleriyle örtülmüş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the blessing means adding political dominion to success in prophethood, granting both religious and worldly favors.
rows.anchor: risaletteki muvaffakiyetine bir de mülk zammolunmak gibi dînî ve dünyevî nimetler ifâza eyleye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path guides the Prophet directly to God's pleasure in fulfilling revelation and carrying out the duties of leadership.
rows.anchor: gerek risaletin îfâsında ve gerek riyasetin merasimini edâda doğrudan doğru Allah’ın rızâsına erdiren bir istikāmet yoluna çıkara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That path is independent administration of Islamic affairs under true law, free from outside influence, making the Muslim community a model for humanity as in 2:143.
rows.anchor: umûr-i İslâm’ın ağyâr te’sîrâtından âzâde olarak mahza şer‘-i hak dairesinde bi’l-istiklâl idaresi yoludur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uprightness already existed before the conquest, but recognized independence at home and abroad gave guidance new clarity and splendor and began a period of growth described in 41:53.
rows.anchor: fetihten sonra istiklâlin resmen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised mighty help is an unmatched victory and is explained by the promise to make Islam prevail over every religion.
rows.anchor: Allah seni azîz bir nasr ile, yani misli bulunmaz bînazîr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage next states that God sent tranquility down into the believers' hearts.
rows.anchor: mü’minlerin kalblerine o sekîneti indirdi.
